newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta bank deposits grew 4.1 pct in Q1 97-c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Malta bank deposits grew 4.1 pct in Q1 97-c.bank.

text.p: The consolidated balance sheet of Malta's five deposit banks expanded by 4.1 percent during the first quarter of 1997 to show total assets/liabilities of 2,230.5 million Malta pounds at the end of March, the Malta Central Bank said in its Quarterly Review publication.
This rate of growth was marginally lower than the 4.3 percent rise seen in the last quarter of 1996 but up steeply from one percent increase seen during the first quarter of 1996.

The banks continued to finance their activities primarily through resident deposits, which rose by 38.8 million Malta pounds, or 2.6 percent, to 1,535.5 million pounds, unchanged from the corresponding quarter in 1996.
The share of resident deposits in the banks' total liabilities declined from 69.9 percent at the end of 1996 to 68.8 percent during the first quarter of 1997.
Foreign liabilities rose by 32.3 million pounds or 14.1 percent to just under 262 million pounds.
The Central Bank said this increase was attributable to banks' involvement in overseas money markets mainly through the active use of repurchase agreements with foreign banks.

Local lending by the deposit banks rose by 52.6 million pounds (4.9 percent) to 1,132.1 million pounds during the first quarter of 1997. This was higher than the 1.9 percent growth rate seen in the previous quarter but down from a 5.8 percent rise in the first quarter of 1996.
